overview.description: A gradient thermocycler runs the same reaction at a different temperature per column, testing up to 12 annealing temperatures at once. Without one, you can run the same reaction day after day - a gradient cycler is a quality-of-life upgrade worth scouting university surplus for.
objectives: use a temperature gradient to optimise annealing
interpret a gradient gel to pick the best Tm
substitute day-by-day runs if you lack a gradient cycler

instructions.title: Set the gradient
instructions.description: Program a temperature gradient spanning ~5-10C around your predicted Tm.

instructions.title: Run & gel
instructions.description: Run all columns, then load each on a gel side by side.

instructions.title: Pick the winner
instructions.description: Choose the temperature giving the strongest specific band with the least non-specific product.

submission.description: Submit a gradient gel image and state the optimal annealing temperature you'll use going forward.
